mainTopic: Who counts as a משומד or מין and how they are treated, and whether a non-Jew may perform מילה on a Jew.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: מינין, מסורות and משומדים may be lowered into a pit and are not pulled out. רבי יוחנן objects that the Torah includes a משומד in השבת אבידה, so he removes the word משומד. The גמרא explains that for רבי אבהו, someone who sins להכעיס is already a מין. רב אחא and רבינא then argue over whether a spiteful sinner is a מין or a משומד. A ברייתא about eating a flea is answered by saying that wanting to taste something forbidden counts as desire. The גמרא then explains that 'not raised' allows quietly removing a way out of the pit, such as a ledge, the opening or a ladder. A new ברייתא about מילה follows. רבי מאיר forbids a non-Jew to circumcise a Jew, while the חכמים allow it if others are watching. A contradiction from another ברייתא about a כותי and an ארמאי leads to swapping the names, then taking that swap back. The new answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: heretics, informers and apostates are lowered, not raised
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that מינין, מסורות and משומדים may be lowered into a pit and are not raised out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and we do not lower them into a pit. But heretics, informers and apostates are lowered into a pit and are not raised out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of a ברייתא that רבי אבהו recited before רבי יוחנן. It lists people who are treated harshly when it comes to a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group mentioned earlier is treated neutrally: we neither help them nor harm them. This last group (מינין, מסורות, משומדים) is treated much more harshly: we may even lower them in, and we do not pull them out. This harsh line is what רבי יוחנן is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: We lower them down into a pit.
We raise them up out of a pit.
Informers who hand Jews over to hostile authorities.
Apostates, Jews who have broken away from keeping the Torah.

phrases.english: and one may not lower them into a pit.
But the heretics and the informers
and the apostates
are lowered into a pit, and are not raised out of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַמִּינִין וְהַמָּסוֹרוֹת וְהַמְשׁוּמָּדִים מוֹרִידִין וְלֹא מַעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מינין, מסורות and משומדים may be lowered into a pit and are not raised out of it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן objects and removes the word משומד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out that a משומד is included in השבת אבידה, so it makes no sense to push him into a pit. He tells רבי אבהו to take משומד out of the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I teach that 'every lost item of your brother' comes to include the apostate, and you say we lower him into a pit? Remove 'apostate' from here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the ברייתא. He says the word משומד does not belong in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about returning lost items says 'every lost item of your brother.' The word 'every' teaches that even a משומד's lost item must be returned. If we must return his property, we surely cannot be allowed to harm him. So רבי יוחנן fixes the ברייתא by deleting משומד.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, meaning a word in the פסוק adds another case.
Remove from here, meaning delete this word from the text.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a משומד stops being a משומד. He is only saying a משומד does not get the harsh 'lower into a pit' treatment, because the Torah still calls him 'your brother' for lost items.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is speaking to רבי אבהו, who just recited this ברייתא.

phrases.english: I teach
"with every lost item of your brother"
to include the apostate,
and you say that we lower him into a pit?
Remove 'apostate' from here!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה לְכׇל אֲבֵדַת אָחִיךָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַמְשׁוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inclusion of משומד in the ברייתא of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that משומדים may be lowered into a pit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah includes a משומד in השבת אבידה, so he is still treated as 'your brother.' He cannot be someone we are allowed to harm.

steps.title: Why not split between two kinds of משומד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אבהו did not answer by saying the פסוק means a משומד לתיאבון and the ברייתא means a משומד להכעיס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him answer him: here it is speaking of an apostate who eats non-kosher meat out of appetite, and there it is speaking of an apostate who eats non-kosher meat to spite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way רבי אבהו could have saved his ברייתא without deleting a word. It is asking why he did not say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of משומד. One eats נבילות because he wants the food (לתיאבון). The other eats it to rebel against the Torah (להכעיס). The פסוק could include the first kind and the ברייתא could mean the second. That would leave the ברייתא's wording intact.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him answer him; why didn't he answer this way?
Meat from animals not properly slaughtered; non-kosher meat.
To spite, as an act of rebellion.

phrases.english: And let him answer him:
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: why didn't רבי אבהו answer רבי יוחנן like this?

phrases.english: Here, it is speaking of an apostate
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק about lost items.

phrases.english: who eats non-kosher meat out of appetite,
there, it is speaking of an apostate
who eats non-kosher meat to spite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the text needed to be changed in Step 2 when a split answer was available.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's acceptance of deleting משומד from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Splitting into two kinds of משומד would settle the contradiction without changing the text, and that is normally preferred.

steps.title: Eating to spite makes one a מין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו holds that someone who eats נבילות להכעיס is already a מין. The ברייתא's word משומד can therefore only mean the לתיאבון type.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: one who eats non-kosher meat to spite is a heretic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the split would not work for רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אבהו's view, the spiteful sinner is not called a משומד at all. He is a מין, and the ברייתא already lists מינין. So the word משומד in the ברייתא must mean the appetite sinner. The פסוק includes that same person in השבת אבידה, so the word had to be deleted.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his view.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אבהו, sinning לתיאבון makes one a משומד, who is still included in השבת אבידה. Sinning להכעיס makes one a מין.

phrases.english: He holds:
one who eats non-kosher meat to spite
is a heretic.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר אוֹכֵל נְבֵילוֹת לְהַכְעִיס מִין הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: the spiteful sinner falls under מין, not משומד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא's משומד could mean the spiteful sinner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spiteful sinner is a מין and is already covered by that word. So the ברייתא's משומד must be the appetite sinner, and that word must be removed.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא argue: first view
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about how to define a משומד. One holds that sinning לתיאבון makes one a משומד and sinning להכעיס makes one a מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about the apostate that רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says: out of appetite he is an apostate; to spite he is a heretic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute about how to define a משומד. Here we hear the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first opinion matches what the גמרא just said in רבי אבהו's name. Sinning out of desire makes one a משומד. Sinning to rebel makes one a מין.

phrases.english: It was stated regarding an apostate:
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree.
One says:
one who sins out of appetite is an apostate;
one who sins to spite is a heretic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר מְשׁוּמָּד פְּלִיגִי רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an אמוראים dispute about the definition that Step 4 used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: sinning לתיאבון makes one a משומד; sinning להכעיס makes one a מין.

steps.title: Second view: a מין is an idol worshipper
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion holds that even sinning להכעיס is only being a משומד. A מין is specifically someone who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one says: even one who sins to spite is also an apostate. Rather, who is a heretic? This is one who worships idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion widens the meaning of משומד and narrows the meaning of מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this opinion, sinning להכעיס does not make one a מין. He is still a משומד. The title מין is kept only for someone who worships עבודה זרה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about defining a מין. One view says it is anyone who sins להכעיס. The other says it is only someone who worships עבודה זרה; a spiteful sinner is just a משומד.

phrases.english: And one says:
even one who sins to spite is also an apostate.
Rather, who is a heretic?
This is one who worships idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ לְהַכְעִיס נָמֵי מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the dispute begun in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second view: even sinning להכעיס makes one a משומד; only someone who worships עבודה זרה is a מין.

steps.title: Eating a single flea makes one a משומד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that sinning להכעיס makes one a מין. A ברייתא calls someone who eats a flea or mosquito a משומד, even though nobody eats a bug for pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא: If someone ate one flea or one mosquito, he is a משומד. But here it must be להכעיס, and still the ברייתא calls him a משומד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack the opinion from step 5. That opinion says sinning להכעיס makes a person a מין, not a משומד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody eats a flea because it tastes good, so eating one looks like sinning just to defy. If that is להכעיס, step 5's opinion should call him a מין. Yet the ברייתא calls him only a משומד.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If one ate a single flea
phrases.notes: This challenges the opinion in step 5, that sinning להכעיס makes someone a מין.

phrases.english: or a single mosquito,
he is a משומד.
But here, it is surely to show defiance,
and yet it teaches that he is a משומד!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition from step 5 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that sinning להכעיס makes one a מין rather than a משומד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating a flea can only be להכעיס, yet the ברייתא calls the eater a משומד. This contradicts the claim that להכעיס makes one a מין.

steps.title: He wanted to taste something forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The flea-eater is driven by a desire to taste forbidden food. That makes it a kind of תיאבון, not pure defiance.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he wants to taste the taste of something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. The flea-eater is not acting להכעיס. He is curious to taste what it feels like to eat something אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The desire is not for the bug's flavor but for the experience of eating something forbidden. That desire still counts as לתיאבון. So he is rightly called a משומד, and step 5's opinion stands.

phrases.english: There, he wants to taste the taste of something forbidden.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the motive is desire, not defiance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating a flea must be להכעיס, since it gives no pleasure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The desire to taste something forbidden counts as תיאבון, so the eater is a משומד.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who sins out of curiosity to taste something forbidden counts as sinning לתיאבון. He is a משומד, not a מין.

steps.title: Why say 'not raised' if they may be pushed down?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא of 'מורידין ולא מעלין.' If one may actively push them down, why does the ברייתא also need to say one does not raise them up?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: They are lowered but not raised. Now, if we actively lower them, is it necessary to say we don't raise them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original ברייתא about who may be lowered into a pit. It points out that the second half seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing someone into a pit is a much stronger act than simply not pulling him out. If the strong act is allowed, the weak one obviously is too. So 'not raised' seems to add nothing, and the גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: They are raised (out of a pit)
Now that [the bigger thing is true], is [the smaller thing] needed?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: מוֹרִידִין אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲלִין.
phrases.english: The Master said: They are lowered but not raised.
phrases.notes: This quotes the earlier ברייתא about מינין, informers and משומדים.

phrases.english: Now, if we actively lower them,
is it necessary to say we don't raise them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מוֹרִידִין אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the definition of משומד and returns to analyze the wording of the original ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ולא מעלין' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stronger act (pushing down) is permitted, stating the weaker point (not raising) seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Scraping away a foothold in the pit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר חמא, quoting רב ששת, answers that 'not raised' teaches something more: one may scrape off a ledge in the pit, using an excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר חמא said in the name of רב ששת: It is needed to teach that if there was a step in the pit, he scrapes it away. He uses an excuse and says: So that animals won't climb down on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to step 9. 'Not raised' teaches that one may remove a ledge the man could use to climb out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase covers more than just not helping him up. It also lets a person remove an existing way out. He does it quietly, giving the innocent-sounding excuse that he is keeping animals from going down.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for (a special case)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Ḥama said that Rav Sheshet said:
It is needed only
to teach that if there was a step in the pit, he scrapes it away,
since he takes an excuse for himself and says:
So that animals won't go down on it.
phrases.notes: This is the excuse he gives out loud, so his real aim isn't obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֹא נִצְרְכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the rule: 'not raised' includes removing an existing way out.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that one may scrape away a ledge, giving an excuse.

steps.title: Covering the mouth of the well with a stone
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף give a different case: one may cover the well's opening with a stone that is there, with the excuse that one's animals need to cross.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: It is needed to teach that if there was a stone at the mouth of the well, he covers it, saying: So my animals can cross over it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to step 9. 'Not raised' teaches that one may cover the opening of the well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first answer, this is a quiet way to block the exit. The difference is the method: instead of scraping a ledge inside, he closes the top. The excuse of letting animals pass hides his real purpose.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:
It is needed only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה אֶבֶן עַל פִּי הַבְּאֵר,
phrases.english: to teach that if there was a stone at the mouth of the well,
he covers it, saying: It's so my animals can cross over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לֹא נִצְרְכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 9, alongside step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the rule to a different indirect method.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that one may cover the well's opening, giving an excuse.

steps.title: Taking away the ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a third case: one may take out a ladder that is in the pit, saying he needs it to bring his son down from the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It teaches that if there was a ladder, he removes it, saying: I need it to bring my son down from the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to step 9. 'Not raised' teaches that one may take away a ladder the man could climb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three answers share one idea. 'Not raised' allows removing an existing way out, as long as it is done with a believable excuse. Each answer just gives a different example of how.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Not raised' teaches more than 'don't help.' One may even remove an existing way out (a ledge, an open top, a ladder), using a reasonable excuse.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אָמַר: שֶׁאִם הָיָה סוּלָּם, מְסַלְּקוֹ,
phrases.english: Ravina said: That if there was a ladder, he removes it,
saying: I need it to bring my son down from the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: שֶׁאִם הָיָה סוּלָּם, מְסַלְּקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 9, parallel to steps 10 and 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the rule to another indirect method.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that one may remove a ladder, giving an excuse.

steps.title: Circumcision between a Jew and a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a Jew may circumcise a non-Jew only to make him a גר, not to cure a worm. A non-Jew may not circumcise a Jew, because non-Jews are suspected of שפיכות דמים. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A Jew may circumcise a non-Jew for the sake of conversion. This excludes doing it to remove a worm, which is not allowed. A non-Jew may not circumcise a Jew, because they are suspected of bloodshed. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about מילה between a Jew and a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew may do מילה on a non-Jew only for the sake of גירות. Doing it as medical treatment, to remove a worm, is excluded. In the other direction, a non-Jew may not do מילה on a Jew, because of the fear that he might harm him. The closing words 'דברי רבי מאיר' hint that others may disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A worm (a medical condition in the foreskin)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יִשְׂרָאֵל מָל אֶת הַגּוֹי לְשׁוּם גֵּר,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A Jew may circumcise a non-Jew for the sake of conversion,
which excludes doing it to remove a worm, which is not allowed;
phrases.notes: Here the מילה would be a medical treatment, not part of becoming a גר.

phrases.english: but a non-Jew may not circumcise a Jew,
because they are suspected of bloodshed.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יִשְׂרָאֵל מָל אֶת הַגּוֹי לְשׁוּם גֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the rules of מילה between a Jew and a non-Jew.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may circumcise a non-Jew for גירות but not to cure a worm. A non-Jew may not circumcise a Jew, because of the suspicion of שפיכות דמים (according to רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The Rabbis allow a non-Jew to circumcise with others watching; רבי מאיר does not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the חכמים say a non-Jew may circumcise a Jew if others are standing over him. רבי מאיר says not even then, because he might tilt the knife and maim the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: a non-Jew may circumcise a Jew when others are standing over him, but not when the two of them are alone. And רבי מאיר says: even when others are standing over him it is also not allowed, because sometimes he may tilt the knife and leave the person with his organ cut off.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It brings the view of the חכמים and then gives רבי מאיר's reason for being stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree there is a danger of harm. The חכמים think people watching are enough protection. רבי מאיר says watchers cannot stop a quick tilt of the knife, so it is never allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing over him, watching what he does
Just the two of them alone
One whose organ was cut off and who can no longer father children

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
A non-Jew may circumcise a Jew
when others are standing over him,
but when they are alone together, no.
And Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֲחֵרִים עוֹמְדִים עַל גַּבּוֹ נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: Even when others are standing over him, it is also not allowed,
because sometimes he tilts the knife on him
and makes him one whose organ is cut off.
phrases.notes: The child would no longer be able to father children.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: גּוֹי מָל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 13, adding the חכמים's view and רבי מאיר's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: a non-Jew may circumcise a Jew only with others watching. רבי מאיר: never, since he could tilt the knife and maim the child.

steps.title: Another ברייתא seems to show רבי מאיר prefers a non-Jewish doctor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר really forbids a non-Jew from circumcising. Another ברייתא says that in a city with no Jewish doctor, רבי מאיר prefers the ארמאי over the כותי, and רבי יהודה says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold that a non-Jew may not circumcise? But there is a contradiction: in a city with no Jewish doctor, but with a כותי doctor and an ארמאי doctor, let the ארמאי circumcise and not the כותי. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: let the כותי circumcise and not the ארמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's view from step 14 by quoting a different ברייתא where he seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 רבי מאיר said a non-Jew may never circumcise a Jew. Here he picks the ארמאי, a non-Jew, over the כותי. So his two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction between two sources
Doctor; here, the one who does the circumcision
A Samaritan, partly treated as Jewish
Literally an Aramean; here it just means a non-Jew

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two people. The כותי is a Samaritan, who keeps some Jewish practices. The ארמאי is a regular non-Jew, which is exactly the person רבי מאיר forbade in step 14.

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Meir hold that a non-Jew may not?
And they raised a contradiction:
A city that has no Jewish doctor

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ רוֹפֵא כּוּתִי וְרוֹפֵא אַרְמַאי —
phrases.english: but has a Samaritan doctor and an Aramean doctor:
let the Aramean circumcise, and let the Samaritan not circumcise,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Let the Samaritan circumcise, and let the Aramean not circumcise!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר גּוֹי לָא? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי מאיר's opinion stated in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a non-Jew may never circumcise a Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא has רבי מאיר choosing the non-Jewish ארמאי over the כותי, which means he does let a non-Jew circumcise.

steps.title: Switch the names in the second ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reversing the opinions: רבי מאיר prefers the כותי, and רבי יהודה prefers the ארמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it. רבי מאיר says: let the כותי circumcise and not the ארמאי. רבי יהודה says: the ארמאי and not the כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying the names in the second ברייתא should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are swapped, רבי מאיר chooses the כותי and does not let the non-Jew circumcise, which fits step 14. But now רבי יהודה is the one who lets the ארמאי circumcise.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, switch who said what

phrases.english: Reverse it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יָמוּל כּוּתִי וְלֹא אַרְמַאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: let the Samaritan circumcise, and not the Aramean,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַרְמַאי וְלֹא כּוּתִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the Aramean, and not the Samaritan.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the attributions in the challenging ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר prefers a non-Jewish ארמאי, which contradicts step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read that רבי מאיר prefers the כותי, so he never lets a non-Jew circumcise, and the contradiction goes away.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה learns from a פסוק that a non-Jew's circumcision is invalid
steps.stepSummary: After the switch, רבי יהודה lets the ארמאי circumcise. The גמרא asks how that can be, since another ברייתא has רבי יהודה learning from 'ואתה את בריתי תשמר' that circumcision by a non-Jew is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that an ארמאי is fine? But it was taught: רבי יהודה says, from where do we know that circumcision done by a non-Jew is invalid? As it says: 'And you shall keep My covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The swap from step 16 creates a new problem, and the גמרא now challenges רבי יהודה. This step sets up a question that the גמרא will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping the names fixed רבי מאיר but moved the problem to רבי יהודה. Now he seems to allow a non-Jew, yet elsewhere he says a non-Jew's circumcision is not valid at all. Only אברהם and his children are commanded to keep the ברית, so only they can perform it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it is allowed
My covenant; here it means the ברית מילה

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַרְמַאי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yehuda hold that an Aramean is fine?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
From where do we know that circumcision by a non-Jew is invalid?
As it is said: "And you shall keep My covenant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:9. ה׳ says this to אברהם, so the covenant belongs to him and his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַרְמַאי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of the תירוץ in step 16, which made רבי יהודה allow an ארמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view, after the swap, that an ארמאי may circumcise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה elsewhere derives from a פסוק that circumcision by a non-Jew is invalid, so he could not prefer the ארמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a fix for one תנא can create a new difficulty for the other, and the גמרא keeps testing until both views are consistent.

steps.title: Dropping the switch and preparing a new answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא takes back the reversal of opinions and announces that it will explain what specific case the ברייתא is discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really do not reverse the opinions. And here, what case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving up on its earlier fix of switching רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, since that fix caused a new problem. This line is a setup: it opens a new answer, and the exact case is spelled out at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16 the גמרא switched the opinions to save רבי מאיר. That switch made רבי יהודה contradict himself in Step 17. Now the גמרא says to keep the original wording after all, so רבי מאיר prefers the ארמאי. The contradiction in רבי מאיר's view will instead be solved by narrowing down what situation the ברייתא is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. A signal that the previous approach is being dropped.
Really, actually. It confirms that the original version stands.
Here, what case are we dealing with? This introduces a narrowing of the case.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is asking a real question here. 'במאי עסקינן' is the גמרא's way of saying 'let me tell you the exact situation.' The answer comes right away, at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: Rather, actually do not reverse it,
phrases.notes: Don't switch רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה the way Step 16 did; keep the ברייתא's original wording.

phrases.english: and here, what are we dealing with?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because of the problem raised in Step 17, the גמרא drops the reversal from Step 16. It begins a new answer to the original contradiction from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retracting the earlier fix and starting to narrow the case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought we had to switch the opinions so that רבי מאיר would not contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The original wording stands. The contradiction will be solved by defining the specific case the ברייתא is talking about, which the next amud spells out.
